description: Anti-AI-slop design skill for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.
summary: Hallmark is a design skill for coding agents that lints generated pages against the specific tells that make output read as machine-made—the eyebrow label, the single coloured word in a headline, the email signup bolted onto every page—and enforces quality through tiered gates (Floor, Reflex, Finish) where a build may overrule a default only on the record. What pulls me in is the 8 KB theme-as-material design: fifty self-contained files that constrain without prescribing, plus a cold fresh-context reviewer as the final gate, which is basically the observability-and-trust loop I try to build into PenguPool and AgentOn Pocket but pointed at visual output instead of session routing. For Proreerfolio, where a generated résumé has to look like a person made it rather than a template engine, the sloplint approach is a concrete answer to the "it works but it smells AI" problem I keep running into.
